about.title: Mohammed Alagab
paragraphs: A Brand Designer & AI Product Builder based in Riyadh.
I work between brand, product, and system to turn an idea into something clear that people can use.
I start with context, connecting what customers see with what teams need to operate and improve the work.

items.question: How long does a project take?
items.answer: A core identity takes 2–3 weeks, a website 3–6 weeks, and an Agent Pilot 3–5 weeks.

items.question: How does payment work?
items.answer: 50% to begin and 50% before final delivery; larger projects are split into stages.

items.question: How many revisions are included?
items.answer: Two review rounds are included within scope. Any further changes are priced before work begins.

items.question: Do you work remotely?
items.answer: Yes, with in-person meetings available in Riyadh when needed.

items.question: Who owns the files?
items.answer: You do, after payment is complete.

items.question: Do prices include tax?
items.answer: 15% VAT is itemized in the proposal when applicable.

servicesPage.metaDescription: Four service lines: Brand & Visual, Digital Products, AI Automation, and Experiential Design — clear scope and timeline for every package.
servicesPage.title: Four service lines, scope written before we start.
servicesPage.body: Each line has defined packages with scope and timeline. Pricing follows the brief, in the proposal.

lines.title: Brand & Visual
lines.what: Build the brand as a full visual system: positioning, logo, color, type, and ready applications. The result is a system your team can apply consistently, not a standalone logo file.
lines.who: Organizations starting fresh, or whose current identity no longer represents them.
deliverables: Visual identity system (logo, color, type, grid)
Corporate applications and core print items
A practical usage guide for team and vendors
lines.notIncluded: Hosting, paid assets (licensed fonts or images), printing and production, copywriting, translation, and photography — quoted separately.

packages.name: Essential Identity
packages.scope: Logo, color, type, and core applications ready to use.
packages.fit: A new venture that needs a fast, correct visual base.

packages.name: Core Identity
packages.scope: Full identity system with corporate applications and a usage guide.
packages.fit: An established company where more than one person applies the brand.

packages.name: Strategy + Identity
packages.scope: Positioning and messaging first, then an identity system built on it.
packages.fit: An organization that needs to clarify its position before the visuals.

packages.name: Social Visual Starter
packages.scope: A social template system with applied examples.
packages.fit: An existing identity that needs organized application on platforms.

packages.name: Monthly Design Retainer
packages.scope: An agreed monthly volume of visual output with rolling priorities.
packages.fit: A team that needs ongoing design without an in-house hire.

lines.title: Digital Products
lines.what: Design and build web products and interfaces that actually work and get the user to the goal. From scope definition and design through launch and handover.
lines.who: Teams that need a site or digital product serving a clear business process.
deliverables: File handover and training on updates
lines.notIncluded: Hosting and domain, paid assets, printing and production, copywriting, translation, and photography — quoted separately.

packages.name: Landing Page
packages.scope: A single page with one clear conversion goal and contact forms.
packages.fit: A service or campaign launch that needs one strong page.

packages.name: Business Website
packages.scope: A multi-page site with structured content and an SEO foundation.
packages.fit: A company that needs a site that represents it and takes enquiries.

packages.name: MVP / Web App
packages.scope: A first product with core features, accounts, and an admin view.
packages.fit: A product idea that needs a usable version to test.

lines.title: AI Automation
lines.what: Build workflows and AI agents tied to a real business problem and real data. Sensitive decisions stay with people; the system handles the repetition.
lines.who: Teams spending long hours on repetitive tasks or near-identical replies.
deliverables: A map of the current workflow and automation opportunities
Tool build, integration, and testing on real cases
Clear limits on what the system handles and what stays human
lines.notIncluded: Model and tool subscriptions, hosting, paid assets, copywriting, translation, and photography — quoted separately.

packages.name: Automation Audit + Blueprint
packages.scope: Workflow analysis and a written blueprint of automation priorities.
packages.fit: A team that senses the waste but not where to start.

packages.name: Workflow Build
packages.scope: Build, integrate, and operationally test one or more workflows.
packages.fit: A specific repetitive process ready to automate.

packages.name: AI Agent Pilot
packages.scope: A scoped AI agent on real data, with measurement and follow-up.
packages.fit: An organization that wants to test an agent before scaling.

lines.title: Experiential Design
lines.what: Extend the identity into a physical experience at exhibitions and events: booth concept, graphics, and production files. Designed around the vendor, budget, and schedule.
lines.who: Organizations exhibiting at an event that needs a coherent on-brand presence.
deliverables: Graphic system for booth and screens
Support on production questions before the event
lines.notIncluded: Production, installation and printing, space rental, paid assets, copywriting, translation, and photography — quoted separately.

packages.name: Booth Concept
packages.scope: Visual concept and space layout with illustrative visuals.
packages.fit: A near-term appearance that needs a clear direction fast.

packages.name: Booth Concept + 3D + Graphics
packages.scope: Concept plus a 3D model and a full graphic system.
packages.fit: A flagship booth that needs an accurate view before production.

packages.name: Event Branding

packages.fit: An event or conference that needs its own identity.

privacyPage.title: Privacy policy
privacyPage.intro: A short, plain page: exactly what I collect, why, and how long I keep it.

sections.title: What I collect
sections.body: Only what you type into the "Start a project" form: your name, company if you add it, email, WhatsApp number if you add it, the service line and package, budget range, timeline, project description, and any links you send. I also record the page language and the source of your visit (for example a campaign or an external link) so I know where the brief came from.

sections.title: Why I collect it
sections.body: Only to respond to your request: reviewing the brief, contacting you, and preparing a written proposal. No newsletters, no marketing messages.

sections.title: How long I keep it
sections.body: Briefs are kept for 12 months from the date they are sent, then deleted. If we work together, contract records are kept for as long as the law requires.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can request a copy of your data, a correction, or deletion at any time by emailing the address below. I act on the request within a reasonable time.

sections.title: No selling, no sharing
sections.body: Your data is never sold or shared with anyone else. Only the technical services needed to run the site and send me the notification are involved.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: Briefs are stored in a protected database that no visitor can read. Access is mine only.

aboutPage.metaTitle: About Mohammed Alagab — Design × Operations × Applied AI
aboutPage.metaDescription: From building identities to building systems: Mohammed Alagab’s path through design, operations and applied AI. Over 12 years across Sudan, Oman and Saudi Arabia.
aboutPage.name: Mohammed Alagab
story: I began where people see the work: the brand, the image and the experience.
Over more than 12 years across Sudan, Oman and Saudi Arabia, I worked in branding, art direction, exhibitions and brand activation, then gradually moved into operations and project delivery.

I built more than 40 identity systems for organisations across sectors, working with teams, suppliers and decision-makers on projects spanning identity and advertising through to exhibitions and on-site experiences.

principles.title: Evidence before claims
principles.body:
I do not build my reputation on what I say I can do.
I show what I have built, tested and achieved, and clearly distinguish what has worked in practice from what is still experimental.

principles.title: The system matters more than the piece
principles.body:
Identity, product, workflow and AI are connected parts.
Their value emerges when they work together as one system.

principles.title: Automation for repetition. People for judgment.
principles.body:
I let machines handle what repeats and can be controlled.
Decisions that need context and human judgment stay with people.

principles.title: Clarity before execution
principles.body: Before any project begins, these questions must have clear answers:
questions: How will we know we are done?

principles.title: Build before theorising
principles.body:
The best way to understand a system is to build and run it.
I prefer a working prototype, a real workflow or a product you can try over ten pages of theory.

timeline.title: The beginning — Sudan
timeline.body: I started in advertising and design, learning to turn ideas into real outputs while working within time, budget and client requirements.

timeline.title: Oman
timeline.body: Working in the Omani market, I began treating a brand as a system that extends beyond its logo into campaigns, marketing materials and different touchpoints.

timeline.title: Saudi Arabia
timeline.body:
I moved from executing design to leading creative work.
Brand strategy, visual identity, campaigns, production, and managing teams and suppliers from idea to delivery.

timeline.title: Al Khafji Joint Operations — KJO / Aramco
timeline.body:
The work expanded into a wider operational environment.
Projects, exhibitions, wayfinding, stakeholders, suppliers and deadlines: the quality of the outcome depended on how well the system worked, as well as the design itself.

timeline.title: First Value
timeline.body:
I brought together brand strategy, creative leadership and managing work from idea to execution.
The focus moved toward building a clear brand direction and connecting it to the business and its outputs.

timeline.title: Independent Practice
timeline.body:
I shifted more clearly from producing outputs to building the systems that produce them.
Operations, projects, workflows, digital products and automation tied to real business problems.

timeline.title: Operational Clarity
timeline.body:
Today, I work at the intersection of operations, AI and product building.
I build workflows, AI agents and digital products, turning real business problems into systems that can be operated and measured.
Current projects include Smart Field and LifeTent: the first demonstrates automation within a real sales process; the second is my experience of building an Arabic product from scratch.

aboutPage.heroStatement: I design what people see, and build the system that makes the work happen behind it.
aboutPage.storyTitle: From building identities to building systems
aboutPage.storyObservation: Over time, I started to notice a recurring pattern:
storyQuote: The problem is rarely the idea.
It is the system that turns the idea into a result.
newQuestions: What happens after it leaves my hands?
storyBridge: That shift led me further into operations, digital products, automation and AI.
I started building working websites and products, then workflows, CRM systems and AI agents connected to real data and business problems.
aboutPage.impactLabel: Sales opportunities processed by the automation system
aboutPage.impactTitle: When automation becomes part of the work.
aboutPage.impactBody: In one project, I built a sales automation system that processed more than 1,100 opportunities using CRM, AI agents and n8n, turning automation from a technical idea into a working part of the sales process.
storyToday: Today, I see design, operations and AI as connected disciplines.
I design what people see, and build the system that makes the work happen behind it.
aboutPage.storyFlowLabel: This is where I work from today
closingBody: An idea needs a system that makes it work.
That system needs someone who understands the bigger picture and the details beneath it.
aboutPage.closingLine: From vision to systems that work.
